'''Bulls Head''' is a neighborhood in west-central [[Staten Island]], one of the five [[Borough (New York City)|borough]]s of [[New York City]]. It is bordered by [[New Springville, Staten Island|New Springville]] to the south, [[Bloomfield, Staten Island|Bloomfield]] to the west, [[Willowbrook, Staten Island|Willowbrook]] to the east, [[Graniteville, Staten Island|Graniteville]] to the north, and [[Westerleigh, Staten Island|Westerleigh]] to the north.

== History ==
The community received its name from an 18th-century [[tavern]] located at the intersection of [[Victory Boulevard (Staten Island)|Victory Boulevard]] and [[Richmond Avenue]] (the neighborhood's central point), from which a sign bearing a bull's head was displayed. The Bulls Head area was also known as Phoenixville.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oldmapsne.com/item.php?item_id=7516&category_id=404 |accessdate=November 6, 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304042431/http://www.oldmapsne.com/item.php?item_id=7516&category_id=404 |archivedate=March 4, 2016 |title=Old map of part of Northfield and Middletown, Staten Island, New York }}</ref>

During the [[American Revolution]], this tavern became the local headquarters of the faction loyal to the British crown, or [[Loyalist (American Revolution)|Tories]], as they were colloquially known. The Bulls Head Tavern burned down in 1871.<ref>Fire in Northfield, Staten Island. ''The New York Times'', March 2, 1871, page 8</ref>

As recently as the early 1960s, Bulls Head and the surrounding neighborhoods, such as [[Willowbrook, Staten Island|Willowbrook]] to the east and [[Graniteville, Staten Island|Graniteville]] to the north, were dominated by farmland. Dramatic change came soon after the [[Verrazzano–Narrows Bridge]] opened in 1964, opening up the area to residential development. Soon many [[Jewish people|Jewish]] families, mostly from the boroughs of [[Brooklyn]] and [[Queens]], settled in Bulls Head<ref>{{cite web|author=Ken Paulsen |url=http://www.silive.com/transportation/index.ssf/2008/10/our_staten_island_streets_rich_1.html |title=Our Staten Island Streets: Richmond Avenue |publisher=SILive.com |date=2008-10-18 |accessdate=2014-05-23}}</ref> and other west mid-island neighborhoods. A smaller number of [[Asian people|Asian]] immigrants live in Bulls Head. Many of the residents are Italian Catholics served by [[Church of Our Lady of Pity (Staten Island)|Our Lady of Pity R.C. Church.]]<ref>{{cite web|author=Staten Island Advance/Irving Silverstein |url=http://www.silive.com/worship/2013/03/staten_island_church_expands_i.html |title=Staten Island church expands its ministry |publisher=SILive.com |date=2013-03-30 |accessdate=2014-05-23}}</ref>

== Demographics ==
For census purposes, the New York City Department of City Planning classifies Bulls Head as part of a larger Neighborhood Tabulation Area called New Springville-Willowbrook-Bulls Head-Travis SI0204. This designated neighborhood had 42,871 inhabitants based on data from the [[2020 United States census|2020 United States Census]]. This was an increase of 3,561 persons (9.1%) from the 39,310 counted in [[2010 United States census|2010]]. The neighborhood had a population density of 8.5 inhabitants per acre (14,500/sq mi; 5,600/km<sup>2</sup>).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://popfactfinder.planning.nyc.gov/explorer/ntas/SI0303|title=Census Data for SI0303|date=2020|access-date=November 27, 2025|website=New York City Department of Planning|url-status=live}}</ref>

The racial makeup of the neighborhood was 59.5% (25,502) [[White Non-Hispanic|White (Non-Hispanic)]], 3.0% (1,295) [[Black Non-Hispanic|Black (Non-Hispanic)]], 19.6% (8,401) [[Asian (U.S. Census)|Asian]], and 2.6% (1,136) from two or more races. [[Hispanic (U.S. Census)|Hispanic]] or [[Latino (U.S. Census)|Latino]] of any race were 15.2% (6,537) of the population.<ref name=":0" />

According to the [[2020 United States census|2020 United States Census]], this area has many cultural communities of over 1,000 inhabitants. This include residents who identify as [[Mexican Americans|Mexican]], [[Stateside Puerto Ricans|Puerto Rican]], [[Albanian Americans|Albanian]], [[German Americans|German]], [[Irish Americans|Irish]], [[Italian Americans|Italian]], [[Polish Americans|Polish]], [[Russian Americans|Russian]], [[Egyptian Americans|Egyptian]], [[Korean Americans|Korean]], and [[Chinese Americans|Chinese]].<ref name=":0" />

71.0% of the households had at least one family present. Out of the 10,773 households, 51.0% had a married couple (20.7% with a child under 18), 4.4% had a cohabiting couple (1.4% with a child under 18), 16.8% had a single male (1.5% with a child under 18), and 27.9% had a single female (3.9% with a child under 18). 31.8% of households had children. In this neighborhood, 33.4% of non-vacant housing units are renter-occupied.<ref name=":0" />

== Education ==
Bulls Head's schools are the elementary school P.S. 60 and the intermediate school I.S. 72. Most of the residents are zoned for [[Port Richmond High School]].<ref>{{cite web |date= |title=Bulls Head, Staten Island schools - ratings for public & private schools |url=http://www.trulia.com/real_estate/Bulls_Head-Staten_Island/5052/schools/ |accessdate=2014-05-23 |publisher=Trulia.com}}</ref> The Todt Hill Library is nearby, at 2550 Victory Boulevard.

== Transportation ==
Bulls Head is served by the {{NYC bus link|S44|S59|S62|S89|S92|S94|prose=y}} local buses and the [[SIM4 (New York City bus)|SIM4]], [[SIM4C (New York City bus)|SIM4C]], [[SIM8 (New York City bus)|SIM8]], [[SIM8X (New York City bus)|SIM8X]], [[SIM32 (New York City bus)|SIM32]] and [[SIM33 (New York City bus)|SIM33]] express buses.<ref>{{cite NYC bus map|S}}</ref>
